text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered for dedicated-cluster-7 (severity: high) -> elevated 5xx rate for tenant 'fincraft-prod'. Alert: 5xx spike (12% over 5m), gateway 502/504 + timeouts. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/board/dedicated-cluster-7

pagerduty: paging maya (on-call) :rotating_light:

maya: on it. paging into #incidents. taking ownership.

jordan: confirmed from metrics — 5m window, 12% 5xx, error breakdown: 502 (60%), 504 (25%), 500 (15%). p95 latency for the cluster jumped from 180ms -> 1.2s. most errors correlate with requests routed to node ded-node-47.

maya: thx. any clue if this is model-related or infra?

sanjay: quick grep of kube logs shows repeated "failed to allocate memory" + kernel OOM kill traces around ded-node-47. also seeing "kv-cache-write timeout" from the runtime. suspect capacity exhaustion (noisy tenant) rather than model bug. paste logs:

```

Mar 07 03:12:44 ded-node-47 runtime[pid=11234]: ERROR serve: failed to allocate kv cache chunk: out of memory
Mar 07 03:12:44 ded-node-47 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 21987 (infer-worker) score 942 or sacrifice child
Mar 07 03:12:45 ded-node-47 runtime[pid=11235]: WARN gateway: upstream timeout while streaming to client
```

alex: seeing one tenant (tenant-ffc, FinCraft) doing large concurrent streams with sequence length ~4096 and batch size spikes. They also recently changed their client to send longer context. This lines up with kv-cache and memory pressure.

maya: OK. immediate mitigation options: 1) apply throttle to tenant-ffc (reduce concurrency / batch cap); 2) evict/cordon the noisy node (ded-node-47) and failover its tenants to other nodes; 3) route fincraft traffic to hosted fallback while we stabilize. I'll try throttle first (least customer-impactful).

maya: running: `redwoodctl dedicated throttle --tenant=tenant-ffc --max-concurrency=2 --max_batch_tokens=2048 --ttl=15m`

ops-bot: command accepted. Throttle applied to tenant-ffc (policy id: th-8f3b) TTL: 15m.

maya: monitoring metrics after throttle...

jordan: reading live metrics: 5xx rate coming down from 12% -> 4% in 90s. p95 latency trending down to ~320ms. node CPU and memory pressure on ded-node-47 dropping.

ellie-cs: I'm on standby to notify FinCraft. How many requests are failing for them vs global?

jordan: breakdown: tenant-ffc accounted for ~58% of 5xxs in the spike. Their error rate down to ~3% now. Global 5xx down to 2.2%.

ellie-cs: pinging FinCraft with short note: "We're investigating elevated errors, applied temporary throttle to reduce impact, will follow up with root cause and timeline."

maya: while throttle is holding, i'll prepare longer-term fix: either increase autoscale headroom for the Dedicated pool or move tenant-ffc to a different capacity pool. but need to ensure this doesn't cause cascading cost/latency regressions.

alex: we can also enable prefix KV caching eviction policy tweak for that node to lower memory retention short-term. would require rolling change to runtime config (low risk).

maya: leaning to: (1) keep throttle 15m and extend by 15m if stable, (2) cordon ded-node-47 and drain noisy workloads onto others just for the hot window, (3) schedule a capacity bump + postmortem. any objections?

sanjay: no objections. I'll take cordon+drain if you give the go. I'll also run a quick heap/profile on the runtime to confirm memory footprint correlates with seq length.

maya: go for cordon+drain. command: `redwoodctl node cordon ded-node-47 && redwoodctl node drain ded-node-47 --evict-ttl=5m`

ops-bot: Node ded-node-47 cordoned. Drain started. Evicting tenants: tenant-ffc prioritized.

incident-bot: note: draining node will cause ephemeral increased API latency for re-routing; we have fallback policy to route to compatible model variants.

jordan: route_policy change executed: set fallback for tenants from dedicated-cluster-7 -> hosted-medium for failed requests (policy id: rp-914).

ellie-cs: FinCraft update sent: "We applied a temporary concurrency cap and are moving workloads to protect from errors. Some requests may reroute to our hosted fallback causing slight latency increase; core functionality should be preserved. We'll follow up with postmortem and recommended mitigations."

maya: monitoring: after drain start + throttle, 5xx steady at ~1.3% for last 2m. node memory freed, no further OOM traces.

sanjay: i've started a live heap dump job on the runtime for ded-node-47 before we fully reboot. attaching the job id: hd-20260307-9. will analyze patterns of kv cache retention vs seq length.

maya: handover: i'm going off-call in ~20m. sanjay, can you own the ongoing watch and the postmortem? i'll DM the incident doc notes and timeline.

sanjay: taking handoff. will keep alerts on and escalate if 5xx > 3% again. will open an incident ticket for postmortem and capacity recommendation (link to ticket will be posted).

ops-bot: drain completed. ded-node-47 marked for maintenance. Tenants successfully re-scheduled.

jordan: quick numbers snapshot before I step out: pre-mitigation 5xx: 12% (5m). post-throttle + drain: 1.1% (last 5m). FinCraft error rate down to 0.8%.

ellie-cs: coordinating customer success follow-up: we'll propose a few options to FinCraft — reduce client max_seq, adopt streaming backpressure, or purchase dedicated reserved capacity for heavy workloads.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to: mitigated. Monitoring in watch state for 60 minutes.

maya: thanks team. i'll add a short timeline + commands executed to the incident doc.

sanjay: will own the postmortem. creating incident ticket now: INC-2026-0307-ff.

maya: handover complete. signing off. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: reaction :thumbsup: added by alex

incident-bot: thread archived (resolved -> mitigated)."
